summary: Delta 534d7ff..HEAD verifies both blocking STD findings fixed (models-record is a convention-conforming locked/validated/atomic writer with lifecycle tests; tiers.json is emitted from the authored frontmatter with a five-harness parity test) and the SEC hardening sound, but the rewritten init publish loop still carries the two round-1 advisory defects: the final config.json is published with an overwriting os.replace (TOCTOU clobber) and config.json is committed before config.README.md with mid-loop failures surfacing as raw tracebacks, leaving an unrecoverable half-complete bootstrap.

round1_verification.STD-1_no_cli_writer_for_models_block: FIXED (was confirmed blocking): cli.py adds a models-record dispatch with the write-command conventions (USAGE write-list entry 'models-record <json> record run models and report prior values'; die_usage on wrong arity; json_or_usage on bad JSON; default value_flags=('--repo',); shared emit(result) tail; ModelConfigError/StateError mapped to clean stderr + exit 1). commands.cmd_models_record validates the block shape (exactly resolved/source with deep/standard, string values, sources in project/user/adapter) via die(1), resolves the one writable run with resolve_target, and writes through write_run -> state.write_state, which takes the lock, re-applies mutate to the state freshly read under it, validates, guards append-only lists and atomically replaces - matching cmd_profile_record's sibling pattern. The conditional commit_worktree (only when previous != block) is safe: write_state stamps no timestamp, so an idempotent re-record rewrites byte-identical state and the worktree stays clean. {previous, current} gives SKILL.md's resume delta. ModelsRecordTests covers pending write, worktree write, resume delta, git cleanliness and three refused invalid payloads with byte-identity assertions; all green.
round1_verification.STD-2_no_role_to_tier_mapping_installed: FIXED (was confirmed blocking): tools/render.py render() collects tiers from the authored core/roles frontmatter (single source of truth) and writes skill/roles/tiers.json after the roles loop - a minimal additive 3-line diff with no unrelated churn. Verified name==file-stem and a tier key for every role in core/roles, so the map keys match the installed role files; dist/ is gitignored and regenerated at install, so no stale rendered tree is committed. test_rendered_role_tiers_match_authored_roles asserts rendered tiers.json equals the authored map for all five harnesses; SKILL.md:24 reads <F>/roles/tiers.json as instructed.
round1_verification.STD-3_init_toctou_overwrite: NOT FIXED (was advisory medium): the rewritten publish still stages only the random temp file with O_EXCL and publishes config.json with a plain os.replace (models.py:137), so a config.json created between the exists() check (models.py:98) and the replace is still silently overwritten; FR-014's refuse-and-modify-nothing still does not hold in the race window (ENG-26). Advisory items do not bind a fix round; reported again because the defect now lives in newly added lines.
round1_verification.STD-4_init_half_complete_publish: NOT FIXED (was advisory medium): publish order is still config.json then config.README.md (models.py:121-126); a failure staging the README after config.json was replaced still leaves a half-complete bootstrap that FR-013 requires whole, retries are still refused by the exists() check (models.py:98), and only the dirfd open converts OSError to ModelConfigError - a mid-loop open/write/replace failure still escapes as an uncaught traceback rather than the CLI's clean diagnostic (ENG-17, ENG-26). Not fixed; advisory as before.

findings.summary: The rewritten init publish still clobbers a concurrently created config.json: O_EXCL guards only the temp file and the final publish is an overwriting os.replace, so FR-014's refuse-and-modify-nothing still fails in the race window (ENG-26; round-1 advisory STD-3 carried into the new lines)
findings.evidence: init checks config.exists() or config.is_symlink() at models.py:98, then inside the new dirfd loop creates the temp with os.O_EXCL (models.py:132-135) but publishes with os.replace(name, filename, src_dir_fd=dirfd, dst_dir_fd=dirfd) at models.py:137, which atomically overwrites whatever config.json exists at that moment; a writer that creates config.json after the check loses its bytes silently.
findings.fix: Publish with a no-replace semantic (linkat/renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) equivalent or an exclusive-creation protocol) and refuse with the existing FileExistsError path when another writer wins.

findings.summary: init still publishes config.json before config.README.md with no recovery: a README-stage failure leaves the half-complete bootstrap FR-013 requires whole, retries are refused by the existing-config check, and mid-loop OSErrors surface as raw tracebacks instead of the CLI's diagnostic (ENG-17, ENG-26; round-1 advisory STD-4 carried into the new lines)
findings.evidence: The new loop iterates (("config.json", ...), ("config.README.md", readme)) at models.py:121-126, so config.json is already replaced when the second file's os.open/write/replace fails; only the dirfd os.open (models.py:117-119) converts OSError to ModelConfigError, so the loop's failures propagate uncaught (cli.py catches ModelConfigError/StateError/CLIError only), and a retry hits the exists() refusal at models.py:98 against the half-written .factory.
findings.fix: Stage both files and publish them as one recoverable step (or publish README first and make config.json the commit point), convert loop failures to ModelConfigError diagnostics, and add a failure-path test that a retry after a second-file failure succeeds or clearly reports recovery.
